Bhante, in 'web books meditations13 section0046 html 65d2f6' (web books meditations13 section0046 html 65d2f6), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding 'We think that the information we'?

In this section from *web books meditations13 section0046 html 65d2f6*, the master explains: *"We think that the information we get through our senses is our most reliable information, but prior to sensory contact, there are all kinds of things going on in the mind."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.

Rest the mind gently in the rhythm of each natural in-and-out breath.
